claim: The lettering style of the drawn sound word, which carries the whole tone of the moment: brushed katakana is a serious impact, latin comic lettering is a gag, hand scrawl is panic. Same sound, completely different scene.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: sound effects, katakana onomatopoeia, brush lettering
sound effects, kanji onomatopoeia, heavy calligraphy
sound effects, english onomatopoeia, comic book lettering
sound effects, glitched digital lettering, chromatic aberration text

review.issue: katakana_brush and kanji_heavy both ask for CJK lettering, which Animagine renders as illegible glyph soup; brush katakana vs heavy calligraphic kanji will not be separable in the output. glitch also smuggles a global effect - "chromatic aberration text" will fringe the whole frame, not just the letters, so that panel changes the render rather than the lettering.
review.fix: Merge katakana_brush and kanji_heavy into one japanese-lettering option ("sound effects, japanese text, brush stroke lettering") and keep latin_comic and hand_scrawl, which differ by glyph shape rather than script. glitch -> "sound effects, glitched text" without the chromatic aberration.
